proposals.expected_signal: Higher frozen full-sort NDCG@10 if suppressing dominant high-degree item shortcuts improves mid-tail discrimination without collapsing propagation depth.
proposals.failure_mode: Uniformly worse ranking if dropped edges remove too much collaborative signal and the graph becomes under-connected for sparse users.
proposals.hypothesis: Applying degree-aware stochastic edge dropout during graph propagation should reduce popularity-path oversmoothing, letting embeddings preserve more user-specific relative preferences in ML-1M.

proposals.expected_signal: Improved NDCG@10 if an auxiliary contrastive loss between shallow and deep transformed views stabilizes useful neighborhood information while preventing representation collapse.
proposals.failure_mode: No gain or regression if the auxiliary term dominates ranking and forces invariances that blur fine-grained item ordering.
proposals.hypothesis: Adding a contrastive auxiliary objective over residual message-transformed graph views should encourage consistency across propagation depths, improving ranking robustness under fixed evaluation.

proposals.expected_signal: Small but reliable NDCG@10 lift if constraining user/item norm anisotropy improves score calibration across popular and less-popular items.
proposals.failure_mode: Flat or negative result if the geometry penalty over-regularizes embedding magnitude and removes beneficial capacity for strong preference separation.
proposals.hypothesis: A geometry regularizer that pulls user and item embedding norms toward a controlled band should reduce score domination by a few large-norm factors, improving full-sort ranking fidelity.

proposals.expected_signal: Higher NDCG@10 if reweighting pairwise constraints toward sampled unobserved items with high current affinity sharpens top-rank separation.
proposals.failure_mode: Training instability or popularity amplification if the weighting scheme repeatedly over-focuses on false negatives or near-duplicate popular items.
proposals.hypothesis: Constraint-weighted ranking that emphasizes hard sampled unobserved negatives during message-transformed graph training should better allocate gradient budget to top-list errors most relevant to frozen full-sort evaluation.
